clue.text: Bump in salary follows employer's third commendation

indicators.note: a third item is the one in position three, so only that single letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the third letter of the word for the boss
a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: A worker's pay rise comes after the boss offers a word of commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the pay bump after the single letter: P then RAISE. 'Employer's third' reads as a possessive noun phrase but just points at one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is approval expressed in words, a direct synonym for commendation.

clue.text: Little dog with favourite doll

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
a teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: A small dog trots about carrying its favourite toy doll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favourite' looks like an adjective for the doll, but it is a noun in its own right, giving PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet is a figure moved by strings or a hand inside, so loosely a kind of doll.

clue.text: Also, for starters, pal, you are no expert

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning of a meal, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a mate is a friend
text-message shorthand for 'you are'

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend, as an opening remark, that they are no expert either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Also' seems to mean 'too' but only lends its first letter. UR is texting slang, spelt as it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a non-professional, someone lacking specialist skill, which is what 'no expert' describes.

clue.text: Mention on the radio for www.thetimes.com?

definitions.note: a definition by example, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: to cite is to mention or quote; it is pronounced the same as the web word

explanation.surface: A newspaper's web address gets a plug on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: CITE (mention) and SITE share a sound. The question mark warns that the address is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times newspaper's web address is one instance of a website, an online location holding pages.

clue.text: Visionary comic lacking an opening bit

indicators.note: lacking means going without, and the opening bit is the very first letter, so that one goes

parts.note: jocular means joking or funny

explanation.surface: A comedian with big ideas is missing the start of a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the J from JOCULAR. 'Visionary' suggests a dreamer, but here it simply means 'to do with vision'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular is an adjective meaning relating to the eyes or eyesight, a literal reading of visionary.

clue.text: Have a discussion about old and new poetry

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
a standard abbreviation for old
a standard abbreviation for new
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Critics sit down to debate classic versus modern poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it links the discussion to its topic, but it supplies C (circa). Then O, N and VERSE follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk with someone, an exchange of views, which is a verb synonym of having a discussion.

clue.text: Urgent mail periodically turned up at a future date

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top
something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Urgent letters keep arriving, but only get dealt with some other day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as 'arrived', but in a down entry it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Later is an adverb for a time after now, which is exactly what at a future date describes.

clue.text: Terminate a contract — or extend it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to quit a job
second meaning: to sign the contract again and so prolong it

explanation.surface: An employee weighs up whether to quit their contract or renew it.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters mean opposite things: quitting, or signing again. The question mark flags the hyphen-free pun on re-sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigning ends employment, while re-signing renews an agreement; the spelling serves both opposite senses.

clue.text: Artificial Los Angeles street in picture

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture
the usual abbreviation for the city
the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A Hollywood street scene in a film looks fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The city and the street join up first, then go inside the picture. A fake Hollywood set suits the answer nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic, used figuratively, means fake or insincere, a common synonym for artificial.

clue.text: Frolicking in cattery? It's guaranteed!

definitions.note: a whole phrase standing for the noun: a certainty is something that is guaranteed

indicators.note: frolicking is playful leaping about, so the letters skip around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cats playing about in a boarding cattery: that is guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition placing the frolicking, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty is a sure thing, an outcome beyond doubt, which the exclamation 'it is guaranteed' expresses.

clue.text: Firm working to return some money

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: set means firm, as a jelly sets
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A company sets about paying back part of a sum it owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' is not a company but the adjective, giving SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are paper banknotes, a form of currency, so they make up some money.

clue.text: Former City business bigwig

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
EC is the postcode district for the City of London, its financial centre

explanation.surface: A one-time financier from the City of London, a corporate big shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London's financial district, postcode EC. 'City business' looks like one phrase, but the definition starts at 'business'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec is short for executive, a senior manager, an informal match for a bigwig in commerce.

clue.text: Amphibian caught retreating over rocky ridge next to river

indicators.note: to be over something here is to cover it on both sides, wrapping around it
retreating is moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: got means caught, as in got the thief

indicators.note: being next to means sitting alongside, so one part simply follows the other

parts.note: a reef is a ridge of rock near the sea surface
the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A frog caught sneaking back over a rocky ridge by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word for caught is turned round; it then wraps around the ridge and river. 'Rocky' is not an anagram signal here; the whole phrase is the ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree frog is a climbing species of frog, and frogs are amphibians, so this is a defined-by-category relation.

clue.text: Offering assistance to support wife giving birth

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits below, so this part is placed underneath the other

parts.note: the abbreviation for wife
helping means giving aid

explanation.surface: A husband helps his wife through labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The human birth picture misleads: the answer is normally used of dogs. In a down entry 'support' means below, so W comes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Whelping is the term for a dog or similar animal delivering young, a specific sense of giving birth.

clue.text: Drill tries breaking concrete

indicators.note: something breaking into another bursts through to its middle, so one piece lies inside the other

parts.note: concrete in the sense of real, solid, tangible
a judge hears, or tries, a case

explanation.surface: A building-site scene: someone attempts to bore through concrete with a power tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' and 'concrete' paint a building site, but the drill is a practice and concrete is the adjective. 'Tries' is the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run, and a drill is likewise repeated practice, as in a fire drill.

clue.text: Tibetan priest hosting lousy dance

indicators.note: a host has guests within their home, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
lousy means bad

explanation.surface: A Tibetan monk puts on a terrible dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion lands after the priest's third letter; a lama is a Buddhist teacher, not the woolly llama.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a Brazilian partner dance that was a worldwide craze around 1990, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Hollywood deal-makers are primarily males

indicators.note: primarily means first and foremost, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
gents are gentlemen

explanation.surface: A claim that film-industry dealmakers are mostly men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are primarily' reads as 'are mainly', but it just yields A.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents negotiate contracts for actors and writers in the film industry, making them its deal-makers.

clue.text: Possible cause of fracture in small lock

parts.note: the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A small lock might break under force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but just joins definition and wordplay. 'Lock' is hair, not a door fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is force on a bone or material, and a stress fracture is a crack caused by repeated strain.

clue.text: Men and girls cast for horror comedy film

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are tossed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Actors of both sexes are chosen for roles in a comic horror movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' fits the film surface perfectly as actors being chosen, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gremlins is the 1984 Joe Dante movie about mischievous creatures, a blend of horror and comedy.

clue.text: Undermine dedicated work led by emergency room

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front, so the other part comes first

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for a hospital emergency room
an ode is a poem often addressed to a person or thing

explanation.surface: Committed hospital work is weakened under the direction of the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dedicated work' sounds like diligent labour, but it is a poem addressed to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, and to undermine is likewise to weaken from beneath over time.

clue.text: Obscene material ultimately has charm, you assert

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so each word gives only its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone defends lewd content by insisting it has a certain appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' seems to mean 'in the end it has charm', but it reaches across all four following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is crude or indecent writing and pictures, a direct synonym for obscene material.

clue.text: Highbrow shindig starting late?

indicators.note: something starting late misses its beginning, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a shindig is a lively party

explanation.surface: A sophisticated soirée that does not get going until late.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily interested in art and culture, close in sense to highbrow or pretentious.

clue.text: I kick up a fuss about Ruth's mother-in-law

indicators.note: to go about is to turn round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: taken as written
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone admits to complaining about their daughter-in-law Ruth's relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it turns I MOAN around. In the Bible's Book of Ruth, Ruth stays loyal to her mother-in-law Naomi.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is the Biblical widow whose son married Ruth, making her that woman's in-law relation.

clue.text: Distance for example a cart reversed

indicators.note: reversed means put into the opposite direction, so the run of letters goes backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
taken as written
a dray is a low, heavy cart

explanation.surface: How far a cart goes when it is backed up, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The turnaround covers the whole string, not just the cart; a dray is a low flat cart once used by brewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a length measured in yards, especially gained ground in football, so it is a measure of distance.

clue.text: Big hammer finally smashes shelf

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A heavy hammer at last brings a shelf crashing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to describe the hammer's last blow; it points to the end of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is short for sledgehammer, the heavy long-handled hammer used for demolition work.

clue.text: Find a way round with the help of … I don't know!

parts.note: by means through or using, as in 'by hand'
what a quiz contestant says when they do not know the answer

explanation.surface: Someone asked for a way round a problem shrugs and gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis sets up a quiz-show moment: 'pass' is what you say when stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass is to go around an obstacle or avoid it, a verb synonym of finding a way round.
